# agent-build

> A browser library: one button hides a web page and a simulated swarm of AI agent cursors rebuilds it block by block, with selection boxes, sizes, guides, rulers and a HUD that says it is a simulation. Vanilla JavaScript and CSS, no runtime dependencies, works under a strict Content Security Policy with Trusted Types. npm package `@magnoscg/agent-build`, MIT.

Usage: load the stylesheet and the deferred script, from jsDelivr with the `integrity` hashes in the README, or self-hosted without them by copying `dist/agent-build.min.css` and `dist/agent-build.min.js` from the package to your site; the unminified `dist/agent-build.css` and `dist/agent-build.js` are for reading or for your own build. Then add `<button data-agent-build hidden></button>` and keep `hidden`: the script removes it when the page can run the simulation, and handles the click. Options are `data-agent-*` attributes or `start()` options: `pace`, `count`, `accent`, `hub`, `frames`, `atoms`, `pop`. API on `window.AgentBuild` and as ES module exports: `start(options)`, `stop()`, `isRunning()`, `mount(root)`, `addLocale(tag, texts)`, `version`, plus `defineElement()` in the module. `data-agent-accent` colours one button and its runs; `--agent-accent` on `:root` colours the whole page and on a button only its look. `data-agent-hub` can be a relative path; an SVG needs a `viewBox` or a `width` and `height`. Events `agentbuild:start` and `agentbuild:end` on `document`. In server-rendered apps, give the button its own text and call `mount()` after hydration. It never runs under reduced motion and always says "Simulation", in eight shipped languages or any added with `addLocale()`.
